requirements.text:
clamp(x, lo, hi) reads its arguments as signed integers. It returns lo when x < lo, else hi
when x > hi, else x.
requirements.reason: The claim uses signed comparisons and selects lo below the lower bound, hi above the upper bound, and x otherwise, matching the requirement for every input triple.

requirements.text:
gcd(a, b) reads its arguments as unsigned integers and returns their greatest common divisor,
with gcd(a, 0) = a.
requirements.reason: The claim computes the greatest common divisor of the unsigned inputs for every pair, including gcd(a, 0) = a; the output fits in 32 bits, so wrapping does not change it.

requirements.text: sum_to(n) reads n as an unsigned integer and returns 0 + 1 + ... + (n - 1), wrapped to 32 bits.
requirements.reason: The claim covers every 32-bit input as unsigned and returns the sum from 0 through n−1 wrapped to 32 bits, as required. The examples for 0, 1, and 2 match the specified sums.

claims.summary: For every 32-bit input, the exported function returns the sum of the integers below its unsigned value, reduced to 32 bits.
claims.name: Examples.Toy.sumTo
claims.intent: `sum_to(n)` on unsigned 32-bit ints: `0 + 1 + … + (n − 1)`, wrapped to 32 bits.
details: Covers every 32-bit input, interpreted as an unsigned natural number for the list length.
The returned 32-bit value is the sum of that range, reduced modulo 2 to the power of 32.
Returns additionally requires the module to be instantiable and every call in every fresh instance, under every host behavior, to terminate without trapping and return exactly the specified value.
caveats: The output is the mathematical sum over all integers from zero up to but not including the unsigned input, reduced modulo 2 to the power of 32; it is not an unbounded sum result.
The guarantee is conditional on the elaborated claim being true; it does not establish a closed-form arithmetic result beyond the stated list sum.

claims.summary: For every triple of 32-bit inputs, the export returns the input clamped using signed comparisons against the two bounds in order.
claims.statement:
∀ (x lo hi : BitVec 32),
  FVA.Wasm.Exec.Returns Examples.Toy.Lifted.module "clamp"
    [FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 x, FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 lo, FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 hi]
    [FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 (if x.slt lo = true then lo else if hi.slt x = true then hi else x)]
claims.name: Examples.Toy.clamp
claims.intent:
`clamp(x, lo, hi)` on signed 32-bit ints: `lo` if `x < lo`, else `hi` if `x > hi`, else `x`
(tested in this order, so with `lo > hi` the result is `lo` for `x < lo` and `hi` otherwise).
details: Covers every triple of 32-bit inputs, each interpreted as a signed two's-complement integer for comparisons.
If the input is signed-less-than the lower bound, the result is the lower bound; otherwise, if the upper bound is signed-less-than the input, the result is the upper bound; otherwise it is the input.
The selected 32-bit value is returned unchanged; there is no arithmetic wraparound in the selection.
Returns additionally requires the module to be instantiable and every call in every fresh instance, under every host behavior, to terminate without trapping and return exactly that value.
caveats: This specifies the nested signed comparisons in the stated order; it does not require the bounds to be ordered.
When the lower bound exceeds the upper bound, the claim still applies the same comparisons and may return a bound rather than a value between both bounds.

claims.summary: For every pair of 32-bit inputs, the export returns their greatest common divisor computed from their unsigned values.
claims.statement:
∀ (a b : BitVec 32),
  FVA.Wasm.Exec.Returns Examples.Toy.Lifted.module "gcd" [FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 a, FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 b]
    [FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 (BitVec.ofNat 32 (a.toNat.gcd b.toNat))]
claims.name: Examples.Toy.gcd
claims.intent: `gcd(a, b)` on unsigned 32-bit ints: their greatest common divisor (`gcd(a, 0) = a`).
details: Covers every pair of 32-bit inputs, interpreted as unsigned natural numbers.
Returns their natural-number greatest common divisor, represented as a 32-bit value; the result is reduced modulo 2 to the power of 32.
Returns additionally requires the module to be instantiable and every call in every fresh instance, under every host behavior, to terminate without trapping and return exactly that value.
caveats: The gcd is computed from the unsigned natural-number interpretations of the inputs, not their signed interpretations.
The claim states the result modulo 2 to the power of 32, although the gcd of these inputs is already within the 32-bit range.
